title: Fuel Oil Pumps - Suction Capacities
description: Single stage and double stage fuel oil pumps and their suction capacities.

components.content:
## Fuel Oil Pump Types

The limitation of a fuel oil pump feeding a burner may often be the suction side. With higher suction lift the "vacuum" in the suction line will evaporate the light fractions of the fuel oil - and the pump starts to choke.

There are two main types of fuel feeding pumps:

- **Single Stage Pumps**: Consist of one set of pumping gears with limited lift capacity, suited for low-level lifts up to 5-10 inches of vacuum
- **Double Stage Pumps**: Consist of double set of pumping gears, suited for medium-level lifts up to 10-15 inches of vacuum

Higher vacuum levels require use of separate lifting pumps and dedicated feeding reservoirs to the fuel pumps.

## Vacuum Loss Estimation

The total "vacuum" in a fuel oil suction line can be estimated as follows:

- **1 inch** of vacuum for each foot of vertical lift
- **1 inch** of vacuum for each 90° elbow
- **1 inch** for each 10 feet of 3/8 inch horizontal suction pipe
- **1 inch** for each 20 feet of 1/2 inch horizontal suction pipe
